props.gloss_en: the mishna's permission to sell concerns a village synagogue; a city synagogue, since people come to it from outside, cannot be sold -- it is the public's
Rav Ashi: the synagogue of Mata Mechasya, though outsiders come to it, comes at my discretion -- if I wish I may sell it
Rav Ashi's ground: they come at my discretion
R' Yehuda: the synagogue of the bronze-workers in Jerusalem was sold to R' Eliezer, and he used it for all his needs
'your possession' becomes impure with nega'im; Jerusalem does not
the tanna kama reads it from 'in a house of the land of your possession' (Lev 14:34)
R' Yehuda, as the baraita gives him: I heard [the exemption] only of the Temple site
R' Yehuda, as the stam's emendation reads him: I heard it only of a SACRED site
Jerusalem was not apportioned to the tribes
Jerusalem was apportioned to the tribes
in Judah's portion were the Temple mount, the chambers and the courtyards
in Benjamin's portion were the Ulam, the Heichal and the Holy of Holies
a strip went out of Judah's portion into Benjamin's, and on it the altar was built
Benjamin the righteous agonized over it daily, to absorb it, as it says 'he covers it all the day' (Deut 33:12)
therefore Benjamin merited to become host of the Shechina
houses in Jerusalem are not rented out, because they are not theirs
the baraita's ground: the houses are not theirs
R' Elazar bar Tzadok: not even beds
therefore the hides of offerings -- the innkeepers take them by force
Abaye: learn from it that it is proper conduct for a person to leave his flask and the hide at his inn
Rava: the mishna's restriction holds only where the seven townsmen did not sell in the presence of the townspeople
but if the seven townsmen sold it in the townspeople's presence, even to drink beer with [the money] is fine
Rav Ashi to Ravina, on sowing a synagogue mound: buy it from the seven townsmen in the townspeople's presence, and sow it
Rav Chisda: one should not demolish a synagogue until another synagogue is built
Rami bar Abba: there [Rav Chisda's ruling] is because of negligence
demolishing an old synagogue to build the new one from its bricks and beams is forbidden (Rav Pappa; Rav Huna)
Rava: a synagogue -- exchanging it and selling it are permitted
renting it out and mortgaging it are forbidden
why? [rented or mortgaged] it remains in its sanctity
the bricks too: exchanging and selling them are permitted
lending them out is forbidden
this [prohibition on lending bricks] concerns old bricks
but new bricks [only designated for the synagogue] -- we have no problem with it
designation [for a purpose] is significant
that view concerns a case like weaving a garment for the dead
but here [the new bricks] are like spun thread [designated] for weaving
and of that no one says [designation counts]
giving a synagogue as a gift is forbidden
giving a synagogue as a gift is permitted
the forbidder: by what would its sanctity lapse?
the permitter: had he no benefit from it he would not have given it, so a gift is in turn like a sale
articles of mitzva are thrown out
articles of sanctity are interred
articles of mitzva are: sukka, lulav, shofar, tzitzit
articles of sanctity are: cases of scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot, a Torah scroll's container, a tefillin bag and their straps
Rava, at first: the lectern is an article of an article, and [discarding it] is permitted
once I saw that a Torah scroll is set upon it, I said: it is an article of sanctity, and forbidden
Rava's ground: a Torah scroll is set upon it
Rava, at first: the [ark] curtain is an article of an article
once I saw that they fold it and set a scroll upon it, I said: it is an article of sanctity, and forbidden
Rava's ground: they fold it and set a scroll upon it
Rava: an ark that fell apart -- making a small ark of it is permitted
[making] a lectern [of it] is forbidden
Rava: a worn curtain -- making it a wrapping for Torah scrolls is permitted
for chumashim -- forbidden
Rava: cases for chumashim and sacks for Torah scrolls are articles of sanctity, and are interred
Rava: lift the ark and set it [in the opening], [and it blocks the corpse-impurity from the synagogue]
the ark is a wooden vessel made to rest
a wooden vessel made to rest does not receive impurity and blocks impurity
if so, it is not possible [to remedy the priests' entry]
Mar Zutra: worn scroll-wrappers are made into shrouds for a met mitzva, and that is their interment
Rava: a worn Torah scroll is interred beside a talmid chacham, even one who [only] learns halakhot
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: and in an earthenware vessel
as it says: 'and put them in an earthenware vessel, that they may last many days' (Jer 32:14)
from a synagogue to a study hall -- permitted
from a study hall to a synagogue -- forbidden
Rav Pappa's version: from a synagogue to a study hall -- forbidden
Rav Pappa's version: from a study hall to a synagogue -- permitted
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: a synagogue may be made into a study hall
Bar Kappara: 'the house of the Lord' (II Kings 25:9) is the Temple
'the king's house' -- the king's palaces
'all the houses of Jerusalem' -- as they sound
'every great house' is a place where Torah is made great
'every great house' is a place where prayer is made great
the Torah reading's verse: 'the Lord desired, for His righteousness' sake, to make Torah great and glorious' (Isa 42:21)
the prayer reading's verse: 'tell me all the great things Elisha has done' (II Kings 8:4)
and what Elisha did, he did through prayer
